text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Greek fighters will take part in the annual Nikiforos exercise which starts tomorrow.
- Man who expected applause for his attempt to burn the Turkish flag at Tuesday's military parade got punches instead.
- Soldier who shot another at a sentry post after an argument is under investigation for attempted murder.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis calls for a convergence of views before negotiations with the Turkish Cypriot side can continue.
- Russian tanks displayed at Tuesday's parade are a significant boost to Cyprus's defence capability, say experts.
- Simitis receives highest honours from the state, Nicosia municipality and the University of Cyprus.
HARAVGHI
- A peaceful solution to the Cyprus problem should be found within the framework of the United Nations.
- "We will pull down the walls and make bridges", says Costas Simitis.
- Appointment of new chairman of Cyprus Airways is expected today.
PHILELEPHTHEROS

- Greek side's policy on the Cyprus problem will centre in coming months on how to handle foreign initiatives on the dispute, Cyprus's accession course to Europe and the defence doctrine Cyprus has with Greece.
- Trade union officials will report employers who trade and "sub-let" foreign workers.
SIMERINI
- The defence doctrine has solid foundations -- Athens and Nicosia agreed on everything.
- A Turkish Cypriot retired military officer attempted to murder two enclaved Greek Cypriots, says a group campaigning for the protection of the enclaved in Karpasia.
- Cyprus has been flooded with designer clothes rip-offs, say local manufacturers.
